model_output.verdict: An experienced structural and pipe welder with specific processes, fit-up tolerances, and inspection results.
write_up: This is a strong welding resume! A recruiter can see the processes you use, the assemblies you fit, and the inspections you passed. Your resume isn't likely to be what holds you back; how competitive the job is will matter too.

The Riverfront Tower line is the model: it names the job, the inspections, and about 900 welds. The one place I'd add context is the plant shutdown line, where the schedule is clear but the work isn't.

cards.line: - Passed every third-party UT and visual inspection on the Riverfront Tower job (about 900 welds)
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this line. It puts your inspection record next to a named project and preserves the approximate weld count, so a recruiter doesn't have to guess how much work it covered.

cards.line: - Worked nights and weekends on plant shutdowns
cards.cannot_tell: The schedule tells a recruiter you worked shutdowns, but not what you did during them. Add the work you performed so it says more than when you were there.
cards.example: Worked nights and weekends on plant shutdowns, performing [shutdown work]
cards.question: What work did you perform during the plant shutdowns?

fit.note: Your experience points toward structural welding and pipe welding roles. The resume names both your welding processes and the certifications relevant to that work.
